open_points.subject: A03 clock-trap policy representation
open_points.text: `time.localtime`, `time.gmtime`, `time.ctime` and `time.asctime` when called without an argument or with `None`
open_points.question: Which State 3 capability represents and communicates the new “explicit `None`” trigger to `sandbox_runner`, given that the only argument-sensitive policy capability named there is `SANDBOX_TRAPPED_WITHOUT_ARGUMENT`?
options: Redefine `SANDBOX_TRAPPED_WITHOUT_ARGUMENT` to cover both an omitted argument and explicit `None`
Add a separate policy value for entry points trapped on explicit `None`
Have `sandbox_runner` hard-code the explicit-`None` condition outside the data-provider policy
open_points.default_guess: Add a separate data-provider policy value for entry points trapped when their sole argument is `None`.

witness.initial: An admitted implementation calls `time.localtime(None)`, catches any exception, and otherwise returns the resulting year through a conforming output port.
events: The kernel executes the implementation in `sandbox_runner`.
One implementation interprets `SANDBOX_TRAPPED_WITHOUT_ARGUMENT` literally and applies its special wrapper only when no argument is supplied.
Another implementation follows the changed A03 phrase and applies the wrapper when the argument is explicitly `None` as well.
outcomes: The call reaches CPython's `time.localtime(None)`, obtains the current local time, and the execution can succeed.
The trap records a hit and the execution concludes `sandbox_violation` even if the function catches the raised exception.
witness.observer: The agent or owner reading the TrialExecution or NodeExecution sees success in one kernel and `sandbox_violation` in the other.

open_points.subject: A03 explicit-None trap call matching
open_points.text: when called without an argument or with `None`
open_points.question: Does “with `None`” mean exactly one positional argument whose value is `None`, any call whose time argument binds to `None` including a keyword form, or any argument list containing `None`; and should invalid extra arguments be trapped before CPython reports its ordinary argument error?
options: Trap only calls whose positional arguments are exactly `(None,)` and which have no keyword arguments
Trap whenever the entry point's time argument would bind to `None`, including supported keyword spelling
Trap any call containing `None`, even if the complete call has invalid extra arguments
open_points.default_guess: Trap only a valid single positional `None` call; otherwise preserve the release interpreter's ordinary argument error.

witness.initial: An implementation calls a replaced entry point with explicit `None` plus an invalid extra argument, catches the resulting exception, and returns a conforming constant output.
events: A wrapper that tests only whether a relevant argument is `None` records a trap before validating arity.
A wrapper that recognizes only the valid explicit-`None` form delegates this invalid call to CPython.
outcomes: The recorded trap makes the execution `sandbox_violation`.
CPython raises its ordinary argument error, the agent code catches it, and the execution succeeds with the conforming output.
witness.observer: The agent or owner reading the execution evidence sees different outcomes.
